results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 57 paragraph summaries of the reverse outline align, in order, with the controlling ideas of p01-p59 (p20 is not in the spec); no unit is unmatched or out of place. The five opening callouts are not spec paragraphs and are recorded with matched_spec_paragraph null.

results.draft_locus: Zillow: When the Estimate Started to Commit ¶10
results.quote: The buyer-lead flow also changed under an industry rule: since the 2024 settlement of the National Association of REALTORS® (NAR), buyers must sign a written agreement before touring with an agent
results.finding: The outliner marked this unit as two ideas (Zillow's post-Offers lead and agent-tool business; the NAR settlement's agreement step in any portal's tour flow). The spec's p19 controlling idea itself bundles both, plus the pay-at-close inference, so the draft follows its contract; both flow readers also found the NAR sentence out of place (A6, B4). The industry rule belongs with the other industry visibility rules (p23) or in its own unit, which is a spec change.

The other units the outliner marked as two ideas pass: Introduction ¶2 carries the four questions, the uneven evidence and the roadmap, which spec p02 prescribes as one transition unit and which the intro reader found clear; the KEY POINTS callout is the house three-bullet block, not a body paragraph.

Every unit advances a supporting claim: the Zillow units S1/S2/S3/S5, Rightmove S2/S4/S5, REA S3/S4/S5, Idealista S3/S5, CoStar S4, the cross-case and Chief Architect units S1-S5, the comparison and verticals units S1-S4. Peripheral units (TravelTime, the collective claim, Idealista's ownership) are tied to the evidence-limits claim S5 or to a book pattern, as the spec declares.

Each table, figure and quotation is followed or framed by what it shows: the timeline by its dating note and Figure 1's caption (inform to commit and back, current pressures); the engines table by the 'denominator reveals the model' sentence, the published words and Figure 2; the Zillow quotations by the tier analysis and the five lessons; the engineering-posts table by its Pattern column; the RTDF calls by the entitlement reading; the AI engagement quote by 'not causal estimates'; the trade-offs, evidence-limits, patterns, Veldmark and verticals tables by their lead sentences; the Lyon figures by the commit-tier questions.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary (e.g. p09 cause_effect 'these engines also explain each portal's appetite for valuation'; p22 similarity 'shows the same dependence from the other side'; costar contrast 'useful as a contrast because it reached property marketplaces from the other direction'; failure-modes contrast 'Trade-offs say what to choose; five failure modes show what to avoid'; questions problem_solution 'Apply the same tests to your own portal'). Where a section opens on a plain fact (Zillow supply, Rightmove, REA), the subheading carries the declared contrast. The verticals opening expresses exactly the relationship the spec declares; its weakness is recorded under flow_is_followable as a spec fault.

Organising principle: both readers describe evidence, then portal-by-portal reading in falling depth of evidence with CoStar as counterpoint, then cross-case synthesis, then the author's rules and their application, which matches the declared grouping, order_of_importance and problem_solution patterns. Neither reader marks any section's position unclear. Material lost-thread points are recorded as separate failed results.

Every other does_not_know term is given at or before first use: MLS (KEY POINTS), share of voice (KEY POINTS), Zillow Preferred as pay-at-close (engines ¶2), iBuying and Zillow Offers (timeline), Buy yield (timeline), Premiere+ and ARPA (engines table), IDX and NAR (Zillow supply), Homes.com's listing-agent model (engines table, CoStar).

The introduction opens from the previous case's question and states the three traits, the four questions, the uneven evidence and the route; it is none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, dawn of man or book report.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic or body evidence, and does not end on a rephrased thesis alone: it reframes the traits as dependences and ends on a hand-off with a concrete next question.

It states what no single section states ('the three traits ... are three dependences on what a portal does not control', each carried as license terms, the durable property, a decision tier, with the unit of charge deciding the core) and says why it matters: 'review a property portal's contracts, entity model and model register before its technology stack: this case's documented successes and costliest failure sit there.'

It returns explicitly to the introduction's three traits ('the three traits this case opened with': external supply, the home that outlives its listings, data that tempts the portal into bets on a future price) and says what each demands of the architecture, as callback.to requires.

The opening-only reader named the three traits tested against ml-platform's tiers, entity-resolution's property model and listing-ingestion's feed contracts; the four questions asked of each portal; uneven evidence (Zillow and Rightmove detailed, REA financial only, Idealista thin) with depth following evidence; the full route including the cross-case views, the author's rules, the Hearthly comparison, the questions and other verticals. This matches AC-2's expected answer and every roadmap promise. The reader's note that the opening is dense is not a prediction failure.

The cold reader answered the probe as expected: the Zestimate became an initial cash offer in 23 markets on 25 February 2021 and Zillow Offers was wound down on 2 November 2021, 'unable to accurately forecast future home prices at different times in both directions'; the model moves from the inform to the commit tier; before launch it needs back-tests on resale price after the holding period, error on the accepting (selected) owners, capital limits and a decision record signed outside the model team; on-market error ('an easier test') says little about off-market or accepted-population error.

results.draft_locus: Zillow: When the Estimate Started to Commit ¶2
results.quote: **The on-market figure measures an easier test**: a model that sees the asking price (in effect the agent's own valuation) is mostly predicting the gap between asking and selling price. The off-market figure is closer to the real performance of the AVM.
results.finding: This sentence explains Zillow's published on-market figure by how the Zestimate works (that it sees the asking price) without a dated source, and it is the author's interpretation without a 'my reading' marker or an inference label. Every other company fact and interpretation in the body passes the AC-4 rubric: facts carry source and year in the sentence or the timeline, internals appear only in the INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED callouts and Figure 7's 'inferred' caption, and other interpretations are marked 'my reading' (p09, p13, p28, p32, p36, p42) or sit in the Chief Architect's view.
